title: Embarrassingly Simple Self-Distillation Improves Code Generation

primary_categories.justification: Simple self-distillation (SSD) fine-tunes a model on solutions sampled from itself; a teacher-free knowledge-distillation-style post-training method (student=teacher).

qa1.evidence: Quantitative pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6; e.g. 'improves Qwen3-30B-Instruct from 42.4% to 55.3% pass@1'; tables across Qwen/Llama/GPT-OSS 4B-30B.

qa2.evidence: Base vs +SSD comparisons across all models (hatched=Base, solid=+SSD, Fig.), plus thinking/instruct variants.

qa3.evidence: Hardware '8xB200 GPUs', hyperparameters 'AdamW ... peak LR 5e-6, global batch size 32, sequence length 65,536, 2,500 iterations', datasets LiveCodeBench v6/HumanEval; vLLM v0.11.0 (commit b8b302c).

qa4.evidence: Code released and linked: https://github.com/apple/ml-ssd (title page).

correctness.evidence: '55.3% pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6'; pass@1 reported throughout.

model_name.evidence: 'Qwen3-30B-Instruct', and Qwen/Llama/GPT-OSS at 4B-30B, instruct and thinking variants.

hardware.evidence: 'We fine-tune with Megatron-LM on 8xB200 GPUs (EP=8 for MoE models)'.

latency.evidence: No inference latency/throughput reported; efficiency framed as pass@1 quality, not time.

memory.evidence: No memory-consumption measurement; 'free-energy' mentions are decoding math, not memory.

serving_config.evidence: 'All inference ... uses vLLM v0.11.0'; sampling 'tensor-parallel across 8 GPUs', 128K max sequence length; global batch size 32.

energy.evidence: No energy/carbon measurement (free-energy term is unrelated decoding analysis).

rationale: Teacher-free simple self-distillation (SFT on model's own samples) raises pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6, generalizing across Qwen/Llama/GPT-OSS 4B-30B
notes: Apple; arXiv:2604.01193v2 (24 Jun 2026), paper Date April 1 2026. Read PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.01193. Main code benchmark is LiveCodeBench v6; HumanEval (incl. Shell/Python) and CruxEval used as auxiliary probes; AIME/MMLU are non-code probes. multilingual flag left false: benchmarks are not in the MultiPL-E/RepoEval/SWE-bench family.

title: Distilling large language models for code generation via ranking supervision

primary_categories.justification: Ranking-supervision distillation: teacher's top candidate tokens are transferred to a student via a ListNet loss instead of full-vocabulary KL; a knowledge-distillation compression method.

qa1.evidence: 'We conduct systematic evaluations on four public benchmarks (HumanEval, MBPP, DS-1000, and MultiPL-E)' with reported gains.

qa2.evidence: 'consistently outperforms supervised fine-tuning as well as FKL and RKL baselines'.

qa3.evidence: Abstract discloses models (Qwen2.5-Coder, DeepSeek-Coder families) and datasets (HumanEval/MBPP/DS-1000/MultiPL-E) but no hardware spec or hyperparameter detail is available in the accessible text (paywalled full text).

qa4.evidence: No reproducibility artifact mentioned in the accessible abstract; closed-access Elsevier journal (OpenAlex oa_status=closed).

correctness.evidence: Outperforms baselines 'in Python code generation, multilingual generation, and data-science scenarios' on HumanEval/MBPP/DS-1000/MultiPL-E (functional-correctness benchmarks).

model_name.evidence: 'across different model scales, including both the Qwen2.5-Coder and DeepSeek-Coder families'.

hardware.evidence: No hardware specification in accessible text.

latency.evidence: No latency/throughput reported in accessible text; abstract notes 'comparable training time'.

memory.evidence: 'significantly reducing GPU memory consumption' relative to KL distillation (abstract).

serving_config.evidence: No serving/batch/framework/precision configuration in accessible text.

efficiency_metric_evidence.memory: 'significantly reducing GPU memory consumption' vs KL distillation
efficiency_metric_evidence.training_time: 'achieving comparable training time' to conventional KL distillation

rationale: Distills code-generation students on ListNet ranking supervision over teacher top tokens rather than full-vocabulary KL, cutting GPU memory while beating SFT/FKL/RKL
notes: Neural Networks (Elsevier), doi 10.1016/j.neunet.2026.109437, online 2026-07-31 (205 Pt B:109437); not on arXiv. Full text paywalled; scored from Semantic Scholar abstract (DOI:10.1016/j.neunet.2026.109437) + OpenAlex W7172015358. Authors: Nanjing Univ. of Posts and Telecommunications. QA3/QA4 uncertain (abstract-only); memory-saving claim from abstract. MultiPL-E gives multilingual flag.

title: Efficient Post-training of LLMs for Code Generation With Offline Reinforcement Learning

primary_categories.justification: Applies online policy-gradient RL algorithms (PPO/GRPO/RLOO variants) in a fully offline setting over pre-collected code datasets to post-train code LLMs; an RL-based training method.

qa1.evidence: Quantitative Tables 1-3 with pass@1/pass@10 for 0.5B and 7B models on APPS+ and MBPP.

qa2.evidence: Compares offline RL against SFT and base model; 'RLOO with GRPO-style advantages improves pass@1 by 88%'.

qa3.evidence: Hardware 'a single A100 80GB GPU', config 'batch size of 8', 'cap the generated code length at 2048 tokens', wall-clock '<30h (7B)/<5h (0.5B)', datasets MBPP and APPS+; LR left unexplored/unstated.

qa4.evidence: No code/data/model release or repository link found in the paper.

correctness.evidence: 'we report pass@1; for APPS+, we report both pass@1 and pass@10'.

hardware.evidence: 'we restrict each training run to a single A100 80GB GPU'.

latency.evidence: Reports training wall-clock budgets (<30h/<5h) but no inference latency/throughput measurement.

memory.evidence: A100 80GB is capacity, not a measured memory-consumption result; memory only a future-work dataset field.

serving_config.evidence: batch size 8 is a training hyperparameter; no serving framework/precision/parallelism disclosed for evaluation.

efficiency_metric_evidence.training_time: 'under 30 hours for the 7B model and under 5 hours for the 0.5B model' on a single A100 80GB (offline RL removes online rollout/verification cost)

rationale: Post-trains code LLMs with offline RL over existing code corpora, avoiding online rollout/verification cost; largest pass@1/pass@10 gains on small models and hard problems
notes: arXiv:2605.28409v1 (27 May 2026); ICML-2026 submission format but a preprint. Read PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.28409. TU Darmstadt/Hessian.AI. Learning rate not tuned/stated ('did not systematically explore ... learning rates'); QA3 given 1 as hardware+datasets+several hyperparameters are disclosed.

title: Smaller Models, Unexpected Costs: Trade-offs in LLM Quantization for Automated Program Repair

primary_categories.justification: Empirically evaluates 13 post-training quantization configurations (weight and KV-cache; AWQ, BNB, quanto, hqq at various bit-widths) on six LLMs for APR.

secondary_categories.justification: Explicitly an empirical study ('empirical study' in Index Terms) of quantization trade-offs across effectiveness, memory, inference time, and energy.

qa1.evidence: 'we conduct an empirical evaluation of LLM quantization using Automated Program Repair'; 13 configs x 6 LLMs x 2 benchmarks with confidence intervals.

qa2.evidence: Base (full-precision) vs quantized models compared across all configurations; Pareto dominance analysis.

qa3.evidence: Hardware 'Nvidia GH200 Hopper GPUs (SM 9.0)' via 'Transformers inference stack'; six named models and 13 quantization configs; benchmarks HumanEval-Java and Defects4J.

correctness.evidence: Reports plausibility / repaired-problem sets ('solved-set consistency between base and quantized models').

latency.evidence: 'it increases both inference time'; inference time measured in seconds as an efficiency dimension.

memory.evidence: 'quantization successfully reduces memory footprints by up to 85%'.

serving_config.evidence: Bit-widths/precision and target components (weights, KV-cache) via Transformers quantized-cache; 'relying on the Transformers inference stack'.

monetary.evidence: 'operational costs' discussed qualitatively; no dollar figures.

energy.evidence: 'GPU energy consumption (Joules)' measured via 'NVML power sampling'.

efficiency_metric_evidence.latency_throughput: 'it increases both inference time' (measured in seconds)
efficiency_metric_evidence.energy: 'GPU energy consumption (Joules)' via NVML power sampling

rationale: Empirically examines 13 weight/KV-cache quantization configs for APR on six LLMs, finding up to 85% memory savings but higher inference time/energy and 48% of configs Pareto-dominated
notes: arXiv:2606.27205v2 (3 Jul 2026); accepted to IEEE ICSME 2026 (Research Papers Track). Read PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.27205. HumanEval-Java is a Java HumanEval variant; Defects4J is real-world Java repo-level defects (multilingual/repo flag true).

correctness.evidence: 'the accuracy assessed via the HumanEval benchmark'.

model_name.evidence: 'across the Llama-3.2 (1B, 3B) and Llama-3.1 (8B) model families'.

hardware.evidence: No GPU/CPU hardware model stated in accessible abstract (Zeus implies a GPU but no spec).

latency.evidence: Energy is the efficiency dimension; no latency/throughput reported in abstract.

title: CacheWise: Understanding Workloads and Optimizing KVCache Management for Efficiently Serving LLM Coding Agents

primary_categories.justification: A KVCache management layer for LLM serving that adds prefix-aware request scheduling and reuse-aware eviction, implemented in vLLM; a system-level serving optimization.

secondary_categories.justification: Core mechanism is KV cache management: reuse-aware eviction and prefix-overlap scheduling to reduce KVCache evictions.

qa1.evidence: Quantitative workload analysis (CATraces) and system evaluation: 'reduces KVCache evictions by 2-2.6x' and improves completion time up to ~3.5x.

qa2.evidence: Compared against 'state-of-the-art systems such as vLLM' and Mooncake (FCFS/LRU baselines).

qa3.evidence: 'server with 2x H200 GPUs and AMD EPYC 9534 64-core CPU with Tensor Parallelism (TP=2)'; model 'Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct'; datasets CATraces and ShareGPT.

correctness.evidence: Serving-system paper; reports goodput/completion time and predictor accuracy, not functional code correctness (pass@k).

model_name.evidence: 'we use a 32B parameter model, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, for our evaluation'.

hardware.evidence: 'We ran experiments on a server with 2x H200 GPUs and AMD EPYC 9534 64-core CPU'.

latency.evidence: 'improves total agent session completion time by up to ~3.5x'; token goodput, TTFT/TBT.

memory.evidence: Analyzes 'sustained KVCache pressure' and XPU/GPU memory as the binding resource for eviction.

serving_config.evidence: 'Implemented in vLLM'; continuous batching, block-based KVCache, Tensor Parallelism (TP=2).

efficiency_metric_evidence.latency_throughput: 'improves total agent session completion time by up to ~3.5x'; token goodput
efficiency_metric_evidence.memory: 'reduce KVCache evictions by up to 2-2.6x' under XPU/GPU memory pressure

rationale: Analyzes real coding-agent traces showing large reused prefixes, then adds prefix-aware scheduling and reuse-aware KVCache eviction in vLLM, cutting evictions up to 2.6x and session time up to 3.5x
notes: arXiv:2606.16824v1 (15 Jun 2026), cs.DC. Read PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.16824. Univ. of Washington / Univ. of Virginia. Benchmarks are workload traces, not code-correctness benchmarks (both bench flags false). Primary 3m vs secondary 3f is a judgment call; either could lead.

title: MARS: Efficient, Adaptive Co-Scheduling for Heterogeneous Agentic Systems

primary_categories.justification: A co-scheduling serving system (external control plane + agent-centric scheduler on modified vLLM) that coordinates GPU-CPU pressure for agentic workloads; system-level serving.

secondary_categories.justification: Adaptively retains KV cache state only when warm resumption yields a latency benefit, a KV-cache management component.

qa1.evidence: Quantitative latency/goodput results: 'reduces end-to-end latency by up to 5.94x'; mean/P90/P95 latency figures.

qa2.evidence: Compared against FCFS (default vLLM) and ILR/S-ILR baselines across operating points.

qa3.evidence: 'NVIDIA H200 NVL (144 GiB) GPUs, dual AMD EPYC 9355 CPUs, 1.5 TB host memory' and 'NVIDIA H100 NVL (96 GiB)', TP=1 on modified vLLM; models Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B and GPT-OSS-120B; benchmarks SWE-bench/RepoBench/etc.

qa4.evidence: 'Our source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Afterglow231/MARS_preview'.

correctness.evidence: Serving/scheduling paper; measures latency, goodput, and task completion time, not functional correctness/resolve rate.

hardware.evidence: 'equipped with NVIDIA H200 NVL (144 GiB) GPUs, dual AMD EPYC 9355 CPUs, and 1.5 TB of host memory ... NVIDIA H100 NVL (96 GiB) GPU'.

latency.evidence: 'reduces end-to-end latency by up to 5.94x while maintaining nearly maximal system throughput'; P90/P95 latencies.

memory.evidence: Manages 'KV cache capacity' and GPU memory (144/96 GiB) under coupled pressure; 'Extra/Reduced Memory Space' analysis (Fig. 1).

serving_config.evidence: 'We implement MARS on top of vLLM'; 'a single GPU (TP=1) on top of a modified vLLM'; continuous batching.

efficiency_metric_evidence.latency_throughput: 'reduces end-to-end latency by up to 5.94x while maintaining nearly maximal system throughput'; P90/P95 latencies
efficiency_metric_evidence.memory: coordinates 'KV cache capacity' and GPU memory (144/96 GiB) under coupled pressure

rationale: Co-schedules heterogeneous agentic GPU-CPU workloads on vLLM, decoupling admission from execution and retaining KV cache only when warm resumption pays off; up to 5.94x lower latency and OpenHands backend
notes: arXiv:2604.26963v2 (15 Jun 2026), cs.OS. Read PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.26963. Duke University. Workloads drawn from SWE-bench/GitTaskBench/TerminalBench/RepoBench/InfiniteBench (repo-level flag true); integrated as OpenHands backend.

title: Anatomy of a Quantized Agent: VRAM Stability and Forecasting in Code-Synthesis Agentic Workloads

primary_categories.justification: A tightly scoped empirical measurement study (1,920 trajectories) evaluating closed-form vs learned peak-VRAM forecasting models for a quantized code-synthesis agent.

secondary_categories.justification: The studied regime is 4-bit post-training weight quantization (Q4_K_M via llama.cpp); characterizes memory behavior specific to quantized inference.

qa1.evidence: Quantitative: '1,920 evaluated trajectories', test MAPE 2.2-4.4% vs 3.4-6.5%, coefficient of variation 0.3-9.4%, paired sign test p=0.76.

qa2.evidence: Closed-form analytical model vs learned ML regression baselines (B1-B5) and constant-mean baseline; 'matches or outperforms the best learned baseline'.

qa3.evidence: 'a single NVIDIA H100 80 GB GPU', four backbones (Phi-4-mini, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B/14B), Q4_K_M via llama.cpp, KernelBench-sourced prompts (300-prompt suite).

qa4.evidence: 'the full code repository and dataset are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/...' (corpus + AgentK framework released).

correctness.evidence: 'compile-success rate strictly bifurcates by ... backbone (Phi-4-mini 5.7%, Mistral-7B 10.4%, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 36.7%, Qwen2.5-Coder-14B 62.0%)'.

model_name.evidence: 'four LLM backbones': Phi-4-mini, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, Qwen2.5-Coder-14B.

latency.evidence: Focus is peak VRAM; throughput appears only in related-work/baseline context, not as a primary reported result.

memory.evidence: 'peak VRAM consumption' decomposed into weight/KV-cache/activation terms; CV 0.3-9.4%.

serving_config.evidence: 'Q4_K_M via llama.cpp' with KV-cache precision terms; 4-bit weight quantization backbone config.

efficiency_metric_evidence.memory: 'peak VRAM' decomposed into weight/KV-cache/activation; 'coefficient of variation 0.3-9.4%'; forecasting test MAPE 2.2-4.4%

rationale: Measurement study of a 4-bit CUDA-kernel-synthesis agent (1,920 trajectories) showing near-constant peak VRAM, a closed-form model matching learned predictors, and compile success bounded by model capacity not memory
notes: arXiv:2608.15117v1 (15 Aug 2026), cs.AI; submitted to IEEE. Read PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.15117. Nokia. Primary 4b (empirical/measurement) with secondary 3g (quantized regime), following CSV convention of tagging quantization empirical studies with both; could alternatively carry 3m (memory management/admission). Correctness=compile success (full numerical correctness on KernelBench 'proved impossible at scale').

title: FastContext: Training Efficient Repository Explorer for Coding Agents

primary_categories.justification: Explorer models are trained with SFT bootstrapping plus GRPO reinforcement learning using task-grounded rewards; an RL-based training method.
Deploys a dedicated repository-exploration subagent invoked on demand by the main solver (Mini-SWE-Agent); an orchestration-level (multi-agent) technique.

secondary_categories.justification: Returns concise file paths and line ranges as focused context, pruning irrelevant repository content from the solver's context and cutting token consumption up to 60%.

qa1.evidence: Quantitative resolution-rate and token-usage tables across three benchmarks; 'improves end-to-end resolution rates up to 5.5% while reducing ... token consumption up to 60%'.

qa2.evidence: Compared to 'w/o Explore for the same main agent' and across main models (GPT-5.4, GLM-5.1, Kimi-K2.6).

qa3.evidence: Full training hyperparameters/datasets disclosed (Slime/Megatron+SGLang, 3 epochs, batch 64, Adam LR 1e-5, GRPO LR 1e-6, 1000 steps; SWE-bench Multilingual/Pro/SWE-QA) but no GPU/hardware specification given.

qa4.evidence: 'Code and data: https://github.com/microsoft/fastcontext'; model weights released on Hugging Face.

correctness.evidence: 'improves end-to-end resolution rates up to 5.5%' on SWE-bench Multilingual/Pro/SWE-QA.

model_name.evidence: Explorers 'Qwen3-4B-Instruct' and 'Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B'; main agents GPT-5.4, GLM-5.1, Kimi-K2.6.

hardware.evidence: Training stack named (Slime/Megatron, SGLang) but no GPU count/type disclosed.

latency.evidence: Primary efficiency metric is token consumption (up to 60% reduction) and 'marginal overhead'; runtime/overhead appendix but no latency/throughput headline.

serving_config.evidence: 'Rollouts use SGLang with thinking disabled, maximum response length 2048, rollout context length 65,536'; rollout batch sizes given.

monetary.evidence: Audits explorer cost via 'Fireworks 4B-16B serverless tier of $0.20 per 1M tokens' (input and output).

efficiency_metric_evidence.monetary: explorer cost estimated via 'Fireworks 4B-16B serverless tier of $0.20 per 1M tokens'

rationale: Trains 4B-30B repository-exploration subagents (SFT+GRPO with task-grounded rewards) that plug into Mini-SWE-Agent, cutting agent token consumption up to 60% while raising resolution up to 5.5 points
notes: arXiv:2606.14066v3 (18 Jun 2026), cs.SE. Read PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.14066v3 (pdftotext; use -a for grep, file has stray binary bytes). Microsoft / SJTU. Cross-stage study (survey sec-rq6): training (2f) + orchestration (3k); context reduction (3e) secondary. Hardware/GPU spec not disclosed -> QA3=0.5. Monetary via Fireworks $ estimate.

title: Empowering Autonomous Debugging Agents with Efficient Dynamic Analysis

primary_categories.justification: Introduces a code-specific Agent-centric Debugging Interface (Frame Lifetime Trace + function-level navigation) that replaces line-by-line stepping, reducing agent debugging cost/token overhead on repair tasks.

secondary_categories.justification: Plugged as a plug-and-play component into existing agent scaffolds (mini-SWE-agent, AutoCodeRover) to cut tool-call/orchestration overhead during autonomous repair loops.

qa1.evidence: Table 1 quantitative results on SWE-bench Lite and Verified: resolves 63.8% of SWE-bench-Verified at $1.28/task.

qa2.evidence: Six SOTA baselines: Claude-Tools, SWE-agent, mini-SWE-agent, AutoCodeRover, SWESynInfer, Agentless.

qa3.evidence: Hardware 'EPYC ROME 7H12 CPU, 512 GiB RAM, and eight NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs, running Ubuntu'; models Claude-Sonnet-3.7/3.5, GPT-4o, Qwen3-32B; SWE-bench Verified/Lite; '$4 budget per task'.

qa4.evidence: 'more implementation details are shown on our GitHub page [7]' (source and agent implementations released).

correctness.evidence: 'resolves 63.8% of the tasks on the SWE-bench-Verified set'; also Correct Location Rate reported.

hardware.evidence: 'EPYC ROME 7H12 CPU, 512 GiB RAM, and eight NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs'.

latency.evidence: Efficiency reported as API cost per task and resolve rate; no latency/throughput in time units.

memory.evidence: 512 GiB RAM is hardware capacity; no measured memory-consumption result.

serving_config.evidence: Frontier models accessed via Anthropic/OpenAI APIs and Qwen3 from HF; no serving framework/batch/precision disclosed.
